title: Special-fibre positivity of a symmetric cubical line over a trait
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$ and residue field $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Put $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Let $p:H\to T$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Its addition, inverse $\iota$ and identity $e$ are $T$-morphisms satisfying the commutative group identities, and separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Assume its geometric fibres are semiabelian [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres]. Let $(B,r,\tau)$ be a cubical rigidified line on $H$ [def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line]. In particular $B$ is an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], with $r:e^*B\simeq\mathcal O_T$ and a normalized permutation-invariant cube trivialization satisfying the cube cocycle identity. All line pullbacks are tensor inverse images [def-pc-module-pullback]. Write $H_K=H\times_T\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $H_k=H\times_T\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose $B_K$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] and symmetric, meaning $\iota_K^*B_K\simeq B_K$. Then $B_k$ is ample on $H_k$. The fraction field and residue field are arbitrary; no completeness, henselianity, excellence, algebraic closedness or properness of $H_K$ is assumed.

source.place: XI 1.13 / 1.16, trait specialization input, isolated from relative ampleness. Original local WANTED. This is an agent-formulated supporting lemma, including the nonproper generic-fibre case; not a claim of a verbatim transcription. Compare Moret-Bailly VI 3.1 and Lan revised thesis Lemma 4.2.1.6 (the latter only in its more restrictive degeneration setting).

proof.text: The DVR $R$ is Noetherian since all ideals are principal. By [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one] its dimension is one, so its only primes are $(0)$ and $\mathfrak m_R$: a nonzero nonmaximal prime would give a chain of length two. Their localizations are $K$ and $R$. The former has dimension zero and zero maximal ideal, while the latter has dimension one and maximal ideal generated by a uniformizer. Thus $R$ is regular by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Smoothness gives an affine cover of $H$ by smooth $R$-algebras, using the affine-local description in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]. Each is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent], so $H$ is regular. Finite presentation includes quasi-compactness [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; since $T$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2) makes $H$ quasi-compact. Finally $H$ is separated as a scheme by [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated].

source.place: Tag 07NF, lemma-regular-goes-up; DVR dimension and the affine-local smoothness description give its hypotheses.

proof.text: Fix $x\in H_k$, and let $y$ be its image in $H$. Apply [lem-sfb-regular-scheme-affine-line-section-cover] to the regular quasi-compact separated $H$ of step 1. Obtain $A,t$ with $y\in U=H_t$ affine. Pull back to $H_k$; [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](3) gives $x\in(H_k)_{t_k}$ and identifies this open with $U\times_T\operatorname{Spec}k$. The identification as schemes is the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. This scheme is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], applied to the affine $U,T,\operatorname{Spec}k$. Thus we have an affine section neighbourhood of this one point, without assuming $A$ ample.

source.place: Tag 0GML, lemma-regular-ample-family; the chosen section neighbourhood is pulled back by the affine fibre-product formula.

proof.text: The dual $A_K^\vee$ is a finite-type quasi-coherent module: a local frame of $A_K$ gives a dual frame and one generator, by [def-sc-invertible-module] and [pqf-def-coherent]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-twist-global-generation] to this module and the ample $B_K$, and choose $n\geq1$ past its bound. The resulting global sections generate $C_K=A_K^\vee\otimes B_K^{\otimes n}$. At least one generator has nonzero value at the identity, since its fibre is one-dimensional. Call it $s_K$. Put $C=A^\vee\otimes B^{\otimes n}$ on $H$. Its generic restriction equals $C_K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]; compatibility with the dual is the local dual-frame identity. This use of global generation requires ampleness only of $B_K$, not of $A_K$.

source.place: Tag 01Q3, proposition-characterize-ample, (1) implies (7), for the arbitrary invertible twist $A_K^\vee$.

proof.text: Each geometric fibre $E$ of $H$ is connected. A clopen decomposition gives a map $E\to\{0,1\}$, constant on every torus coset since a split torus is connected. It therefore descends through the fppf quotient to the connected abelian quotient in [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres], and is constant. The identity gives nonemptiness. Consequently [lem-sfb-trait-primitive-section-specialization] applies to $H/T,C,s_K$ over the given DVR and supplies a global section $s$ of $C$ with nonzero special restriction $s_k$.

source.place: Tag 031T, lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1, primitive-section consequence isolated in the cited node.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), $H_k/k$ is smooth, separated and finitely presented. Base change of its group-operation diagrams preserves the group identities, and its geometric fibres satisfy the given semiabelian condition. Apply [lem-sfb-semiabelian-effective-square-generation] to $C_k,s_k$. It gives globally generated $C_k^{\otimes2}$. In particular one of its generating sections $u$ has nonzero value at the fixed $x$, by the surjectivity in [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections].

source.place: I 2.6 cube substitution and effective-line square consequence, isolated in the cited field lemma; original WANTED.

proof.text: Expand $C=A^\vee\otimes B^{\otimes n}$ and evaluate the two copies of $A_k$ against their duals. This gives $A_k^{\otimes2}\otimes C_k^{\otimes2}\simeq B_k^{\otimes2n}$, using [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] and the dual in [def-sc-invertible-module]. The section $v=t_k^{\otimes2}\otimes u$ therefore is a section of $B_k^{\otimes2n}$. Its nonvanishing locus is $(H_k)_{t_k}\cap(H_k)_u$, by [lem-sc-tensor-section-affine-open]; squaring $t_k$ changes no nonvanishing locus because its value is a vector in a one-dimensional space. This locus contains $x$ and is affine, since $(H_k)_{t_k}$ is affine by step 2. These statements verify the requisite positive-power affine neighbourhood at each $x$.

source.place: Affine nonvanishing loci of tensor sections, the argument underlying Tag 0890; no ample-tensor assertion is assumed.

proof.text: By finite presentation and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2),(3), $H_k$ is quasi-compact over the quasi-compact field spectrum [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. For every point $x$ the preceding construction supplies a section of the positive power $B_k^{\otimes2n}$ with an affine nonvanishing neighbourhood of $x$. The integer $n$ and the auxiliary line may depend on $x$, exactly as allowed by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Hence $B_k$ is ample.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0GML affine line-section neighbourhoods, followed by generic ample twisting, primitive specialization, effective-square generation and the affine tensor-section calculation. Repair removes the circular auxiliary relatively ample line entirely. Raynaud XI and Moret-Bailly I originals remain WANTED.
